sources.entry: unittest.mock - (Python standard library) A mocking and patching library.

summary.name: unittest.mock
summary.one_liner: Python standard library module for replacing parts of code under test with mock objects and asserting how they were used.
keywords: how to mock a function in python
use_cases: replace external dependencies in unit tests
assert a function was called with specific arguments
simulate exceptions raised by a dependency
temporarily patch module or class attributes during a test
generate mocks that match a real object's signature
summary.what_it_does: Provides the Mock and MagicMock classes, which create attributes and methods on access and record how they are used so tests can assert on calls. Mocks can be configured with return values, side effects (functions, iterables, or exceptions), and specs that limit accessible attributes. The patch() decorator and context manager temporarily replace module- or class-level attributes during a test and restore them afterward, and patch.dict() does the same for dictionaries. create_autospec() builds mocks that copy the signature of the real object so incorrect calls fail as they would in production code.
notable: patch() replaces attributes in the namespace where they are looked up
create_autospec() enforces the real object's call signature
Backport available on PyPI as mock for older Python versions
caveats: Added in Python 3.3; older Python versions need the separate mock backport on PyPI
Mock attributes starting with assert-like prefixes raise AttributeError unless unsafe=True
